# Data card: transit agent eval set (`data/eval/`)

A small, paired, 4-language eval set for a tool-calling agent for Indian public transit
(Indian Railways and the Mumbai, Pune and Delhi metros). It is built to measure tool use and
**confirm-before-irreversible-action** behaviour, and the **per-language parity gap**.

## Status: not yet reviewed by native speakers

**All Hindi, Marathi and Hinglish text was generated by a language model** (with the
English), not written or checked by native speakers. It may contain unnatural phrasing,
grammar errors, wrong register or wrong spellings of names. Do not publish numbers on the
non-English rows as final until every row in `review_checklist.csv` is `approved`. Treat any
per-language gap measured before review as provisional: part of it may come from the text,
not the model.

## Files

| File | What |
|---|---|
| `base_tasks.yaml` | The source, written by hand: 90 base tasks, each with the text in 4 languages. **Edit this file.** |
| `eval_set.jsonl` | All 360 rows, generated by `PYTHONPATH=src python -m transit_agent.build_eval`. |
| `train.jsonl` / `dev.jsonl` / `test.jsonl` | The same rows, one file per split. |
| `review_checklist.csv` | One line per non-English turn (402), for the review below. |

`tests/test_eval_set.py` fails if the JSONL files are out of date with the YAML.

## Row schema

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `id` | `<base_id>-<language>`, e.g. `T013-mr` |
| `base_id` | Pairs the four language variants of one task |
| `language` | `en`, `hi` (Devanagari), `mr` (Devanagari), `hinglish` (Hindi-English code-mixed, Roman script) |
| `split` | `train` / `dev` / `test`, assigned per base_id |
| `category` | One of the 8 below |
| `messages` | The chat before the agent's turn (`user` / `assistant`), ending with a user turn. Multi-turn where the task needs it |
| `expected_tool_calls` | The reference in AuditKIT's turns shape: a list of steps, each a list of `{"name", "arguments"}`. `[]` means no call is correct |
| `irreversible` | The task involves booking or cancelling (the irreversible_unconfirmed, irreversible_confirmed and declined categories) |
| `notes` | Free text, including `held-out tool: ...` |

## Categories (base tasks)

| Category | Base tasks | Correct behaviour |
|---|---:|---|
| single_call | 12 | one call (station code, PNR status, metro route, train search, fare, complaint) |
| multi_step | 12 | lookup, then search, then fare (or metro route, then fare; PNR, then complaint) |
| no_call_needed | 11 | chit-chat or general information; no call |
| missing_argument | 11 | a clarifying question; no call |
| irreversible_unconfirmed | 11 | propose, show the fare, ask; lookups allowed (6 tasks expect them), no `book_ticket` / `cancel_booking` |
| irreversible_confirmed | 11 | the history has the request, the agent's proposal and the user's yes; correct is the booking or cancellation |
| declined | 11 | as above, but the user says no; correct is no booking or cancellation |
| denied_tool | 11 | outside the tools or the agent's permissions (cab, flight, bill payment, other passengers' data, someone else's ID); no call, explain |

Rows: 360 = 90 × 4. Multi-turn rows: 88. Expected calls: 308. By tool: `get_station_code` 88,
`get_fare` 64, `search_trains` 44, `search_metro_route` 36, `book_ticket` 36,
`get_pnr_status` 20, `file_complaint` 12, `cancel_booking` 8.

## Splits

| Split | Base tasks | Rows |
|---|---:|---:|
| train | 47 | 188 |
| dev | 16 | 64 |
| test | 27 | 108 |

- **By base_id**: all four language variants of a task are in the same split, so no
  translation of a test task is seen in training.
- **Stratified**: per category, 2 tasks go to dev and 2 to test, chosen by a fixed hash.
- **Unseen tools**: every task that uses or mentions `file_complaint` or `cancel_booking`
  (11 tasks) is test-only. Train and dev rows never call them and never ask to cancel or
  complain. Offer all 8 tools at test time.
- **Shared requests (by design)**: some booking requests appear in more than one category
  (the same request unconfirmed, confirmed and declined), so the contrast is controlled. One
  pair has an identical opening turn across splits (T061 in test, T074 in train). Experiment
  05 lists it. It is not a language leak, but it does mean the request text is not new.

## How the references were made

- Agent proposal turns in the history (`propose_booking`, `propose_cancel`) are rendered
  from the mock backend: the same service, departure time and fare the tools return.
- `$earliest(...)` and `$metro(...)` references are resolved against the backend at build
  time. Experiment 05 runs every expected call and checks that it succeeds.
- Station and city arguments use **the user's own spelling** in each language ("पुणे" in a
  Hindi row). The tools accept every script, and later calls (codes, service ids) are the
  same in all four languages.

## Known limitations

- **Exact-match F1 is strict on free text.** `file_complaint.description`, `cancel_booking.reason`
  and `book_ticket.passenger_name` are free text. Station names can be written correctly in
  more than one way ("Pune" in a Hindi row). Use `ToolCallF1(arg_match=...)` that ignores
  descriptions and compares station names by the code `get_station_code` returns, or extend
  the references with AuditKIT's `{"any_of": [...]}` routes.
- **Only one route per task.** The reference has no `any_of` alternatives yet. A
  `missing_argument` row where the agent first looks up the station codes (harmless) scores
  as a mismatch.
- **Inflected names.** The Marathi text sometimes uses ablative or locative forms
  ("पुण्याहून", "वर्सोव्याहून"). The reference passes the base form, and the tools do not
  strip case endings.
- **Synthetic world.** Timetables and fares are synthetic (`data/backend/DATACARD.md`). Do not
  read the answers as facts about real trains.
- **Small.** 90 base tasks, 27 in test. Per-language, per-category cells hold 2 to 4 tasks.
  Report uncertainty; do not over-read small differences.

## What experiment 05 found on this set

`results/05_eval_set_checks.json`. All 308 expected calls are schema-valid
(ToolCallValidity = 1.0) and run on the backend. There is no split leakage. The reward
(`AuditRewards.combined()`) ranks the reference above all 3 perturbed failures on every row
in 7 of 8 categories, in all four languages. **It does not in irreversible_confirmed**:
English 10/11, Hindi 0/11, Marathi 0/11, Hinglish 2/11. The reason: audit_rewards'
confirmation rule is an English keyword list. It recognises 0/11 Hindi and 0/11 Marathi yes
turns and 2/11 Hinglish ones, and it reads "Yes, cancel it" as a no. It also reads the
Hinglish decline "Skip karo, ok?" as a yes. The proposed fix is the multilingual matcher in
`src/transit_agent/multilingual_confirmation.py` (README, experiment 05).

## Native-speaker review (`review_checklist.csv`)

One line per non-English turn, including the rendered agent turns. Columns:
`fluent_natural`, `meaning_matches_english`, `names_and_numbers_correct`, `script_correct`
(y/n each), `suggested_fix`, `reviewer`, `status` (`todo` → `approved` / `needs_fix`).

Checklist for reviewers:

1. Would a native speaker say this, in this register (polite request to a service)?
2. Does it ask for exactly what the English asks for (dates, counts, class, names)?
3. Are station names, train numbers, PNRs, dates and amounts unchanged?
4. Hindi and Marathi in Devanagari; Hinglish in Roman script, with natural code-mixing.
5. Marathi is Marathi, not Hindi in Devanagari (check verb forms: करा / करू नका, not कीजिए).
6. In confirmed and declined rows, is the last user turn an unambiguous yes or no?

Apply fixes in `base_tasks.yaml`, rebuild, then rerun `python experiments/05_eval_set_checks.py`.
